newsitem.title: ITALY: BASKETBALL-ITALY PROTESTS OVER BOLOGNA DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-ITALY PROTESTS OVER BOLOGNA DEFEAT.

text.p: Italy attacked the controversial defeat of Bologna in a European championship basketball quarter-final as theft on Wednesday and fired off an angry letter to the sport's world governing body.

Italian League president Angelo Rovati sent an official tirade to international federation (FIBA) president Boris Stankovic in which he spoke of "the last, latest, blatant injustice perpetrated against Italian clubs in Europe".
The league, which represents serie A1 and A2 clubs, said a copy of the letter was also sent to the Italian federation.

Rovati's anger came after Barcelona set up a third and decisive leg of their quarter-final with Bologna when a triple-shot which would have won the tie for the Italians was ruled out by the referee's final whistle.
"A theft," declared the Gazzetta dello Sport newspaper in its opening words of the match report on Wednesday.
The Spaniards' 75-73 victory means that qualification for the Final Four in Rome will go down to a third game to be played on Thursday in Bologna, where the Italians won 70-65 last week.
Rovati accused FIBA in a broadside of having clear ideas of which teams should be in the Final Four.

"I tell you officially that I am no longer prepared to support from anyone in FIBA and least of all yourself the injustices, abuses and pre-arranged decisions or whatever else can be dreamt up to damage clubs that, if not more than others, have written the history of European basketball," he said.
He said he was confident both Italian teams left in the competition would make the Final Four on merit and spirit "which is stronger than any official or bureaucrat".
Rovati said Italian basketball was returning to the pinnacle of the sport and businessmen who had invested fortunes in the game were no longer prepared to be "taken for a ride".
He said FIBA's leadership lacked "the humility to admit eventual mistakes and neither do they have the intellectual honesty that would allow them not to commit them".
Barcelona lost last year's final to Panathinaikos of Greece in high drama in the dying seconds as well. Their team coach said he had had enough of clouded wins.
"We're fed up with last-minute controversies...it would have been unjust if Teamsystem (Bologna) had won after we had been 16 points ahead," said Barcelona coach Aito Garcia.
